# `project`

project

THE BUNDLE MANIFEST (mac.project.yaml). Shape measured across three live manifests — only `planes` is universal, so it is the only required key; `additionalProperties: false` is kept deliberately, because an unenumerated manifest key is exactly the invention this definition exists to catch, and `^x-` remains the sanctioned way to extend. Previously the only bundle file MAC did not define — it was exempted by a hardcoded basename check inside validate_schema.py, which meant the file where a bundle declares its own conformance was itself unchecked. It now carries the three declarations that had nowhere legitimate to live: `profile` (CONFORMANCE.md §2 — what each x- key means; without it every x- key is undeclared debt by construction), `conformance.out_of_scope` (the MAC001 escape hatch — a bundle may own files MAC does not define, but it must SAY SO), and `reproduction` (how the bundle is rebuilt, as CHECKABLE data rather than prose that goes stale — measured twice on <dataset>'s REPRODUCTION.md).

> **5 keys at this level carry no description in `mac.schema.json`.** The place to fix one is the schema, which is its one home; this page is generated and cannot hold the answer.

### `disclosure`

*object* · optional · [has its own keys →](disclosure/README.md)

WHAT THIS BUNDLE PERMITS TO BE PUBLISHED OUT OF ITS OWN DATA. A bundle-level POLICY statement, in the same idiom as `conformance.out_of_scope`: a claim plus the reason for it, made once, in the manifest, where a reader and a gate both find it — never per page and never per concept, because a per-page switch is a per-page mistake. Distinct from `capabilities` (what the container CAN do) and from `publish` (where output GOES): this says what the bundle's own rows are allowed to become. CLOSED (`additionalProperties: false`) so a second disclosure question is a schema change with a record rather than a key somebody adds on a Tuesday.

Its own keys: [`project.disclosure`](disclosure/README.md)

### `runtime`

*object* · optional · [has its own keys →](runtime.md)

WHAT THIS BUNDLE NEEDS IN ORDER TO BE ANSWERED FROM. Previously `{"type": "object"}` — no properties, no required, no additionalProperties — which is to say the manifest's runtime block was ungoverned, and an ungoverned object in the ONE file a bundle uses to declare its own conformance is exactly the hole this schema exists to close. The measured cost of leaving it open: `runtime: {conection:..., credentials: {mode: plaintext, value: hunter2xyz}}` validates CLEAN against the old shape (note the typo, silently accepted) and returns zero findings from check_bundle_secrets, because mac.project.yaml sits in that gate's config allowlist and the key is spelled `value`, not `password`. Closing the object is what makes a sixth key ARGUABLE rather than silent, and it is what leaves a credential nowhere to sit in the manifest — credentials belong in the connection envelope ($defs/ConnectionFile), which is deployment and overridable, never in the bundle manifest, which is not. MEASURED BEFORE CLOSING, because `additionalProperties: false` is the one non-additive edit here: across the 27 mac.project.yaml manifests reachable on this machine, 4 carry a `runtime:` block and their key universe is EXACTLY these five — source 4, connection 4, interpreter 3, model_catalog 3, connector 2 — with zero sixth key and every value a string. No key is `required`, because one of those four manifests carries only {source, connection, connector}: a bundle that declines a mechanism it has no use for must not be nagged for it. A bundle with no `runtime:` block at all remains well-formed, readable, renderable — and not answerable.

Its own keys: [`project.runtime`](runtime.md)

### `serving`

*object* · optional · [has its own keys →](serving/README.md)

THE BUNDLE'S SERVING CONTRACT — how this bundle spells the relations it serves. A CORE key, deliberately, and not an `x-` extension: the serving-name convention was the single most-replicated finding of the eight-walk ingestion experiment, and every walk that tried to declare it reached for `x-serving-naming`, which this schema rejects (additionalProperties:false, no ^x- pattern) and which tools/check_extension_keys.py PROHIBITS as MAC012. The framework was therefore teaching, in a gate's failure message, the one declaration two other mechanisms refuse — opposite policies in one framework, which is a defect to remove rather than a tension to document. Removing it means the convention must have a home the core defines, validates and a gate reads: this one. Enforced by tools/check_served_name_distinct.py.

Its own keys: [`project.serving`](serving/README.md)
